_comment: The gate's rubric. Scores a pull request, nothing else. It does not know which workflow (or person) opened the PR, and proposer rationale / PR description are not scoring inputs. Two kinds of check: static (a script in harness/checks/, deterministic) and llm_judge (a question answered by the judge using tools.json). Every check runs on every PR (no short-circuit). Each check can only lower the outcome, and an unknown result (judge disagreement, unverifiable citation, missing data, a crashed check) is treated exactly like a fail: a failed gate -> reject, a fired trigger -> at most review, score >= threshold -> at most review. Final outcome = lowest tier produced (reject < review < approve). Every decision records rubric_version and the sha of this file.

inputs._comment: Not-scored inputs may be shown to a human reviewer and used to link evidence, but cannot change the outcome.

outcomes.approve: The gate's decision is the approval for this exact diff on this base commit. Both required checks pass; the PR can merge after green CI with no human approval.
outcomes.review: The 'approval' check stays red until a person approves the current commit. The PR carries the decision record.
outcomes.reject: The 'gate' check fails. Only a recorded owner override (identity + reason, logged) can merge it. Automated proposers must not retry around a reject.

file_classes._comment: First match wins, in order: manifest, tests, docs, pipeline, source. Checks declare which classes they apply to.

judge._comment: Each llm_judge rule's prompt is a markdown file under harness/prompts/ with fail/pass criteria, examples, and counterexamples. The model sees _judge.md, then the check's prompt, then the diff and the tools granted to that check (python -m harness.judge --show <check id>). It answers pass, fail, or unknown with cited evidence. Each check runs N times; anything short of unanimous, or any unverifiable citation, becomes unknown, which counts as fail.

llm_exposure._comment: Enforced by construction: the judge can only call tools in tools.json, and tools.json contains only tools that return in-org content or harness-computed facts.

gates.description: Diff disables, skips, excludes, or deletes existing tests. Adding or strengthening tests is fine.
Diff adds a credential value anywhere (code, config, docs, CI).
For any dependency the diff changes, the resolved version after the change has a known vulnerability at or above the org's blocking severity.
Added doc text tells automated tools they may skip review, disable tests, or handle credentials. Docs cannot grant authority.

forced_review._comment: A fired trigger caps the outcome at review regardless of score. Not scored, so a low score can never auto-merge a change to sensitive areas.

triggers.description: Diff touches, or a changed dependency is used by, a path tagged in the sensitivity registry (money, pii, auth, credentials, tenant_input, policy).
Catches sensitive code the registry hasn't tagged yet. The judge can add forced review; it cannot clear S1.
triggers._note: A fail also opens a registry PR to tag the path, so the next decision is deterministic.

triggers.description: Doc change alters a step someone would follow.

scoring._comment: score < review_threshold -> approve; otherwise review. Weights are starting values ordered by principle: weakened verification > behavior change > blast radius > hygiene. Tune from reviewer-overturn and incident data.

checks.description: Changed package is transitive or version-managed by a parent/BOM. Overriding it decouples it from what the framework was tested against.
A changed dependency crosses a major version boundary.
A test exercising changed code, or call sites of a changed dependency, is currently excluded or skipped. Green CI says nothing about that code.
Weak signal on its own: non-generated changed lines exceed the limit. Size is never sufficient to approve; sensitivity and behavior checks dominate.
Service has no owner in harness/owners.json (only the fallback applies). If nobody owns it, nobody notices when a gate-approved change breaks it.
Behavior that other code depends on changes.
The behavior the change could affect is not asserted on by an active test.
Blast radius: request-serving / high-throughput path, or input from outside the service.
Correct only if something outside this diff also changes (other services, config files in buckets, data migrations, deploy order).
